record.original_question: For a fixed compact 3-dimensional contact manifold with a chosen contact distribution, can one define a natural averaging or heat-type evolution on the space of sub-Riemannian metrics that converges, possibly after suitable rescaling, to a nonzero generalized metric preserved by the Reeb field, even when no smooth Reeb-invariant metric exists? This includes understanding whether the discrete averaging scheme or the continuous equation ∂h/∂t = c{uh,{uh,h}} can produce meaningful limiting Hamiltonians with controlled singularities.

evidence.quote: To conclude, I would like to discuss one more problem; it is less precise than already stated questions but, to my taste, is nice and fascinating. The problem concerns contact 3-dimensional manifolds and is inspired by the Ricci flow story.
There is a good chance to arrive to a nonzero limiting Hamiltonian h∞ by a clever choice of the sequences of positive functions εn, cn.
A continuous time analogue of the introduced dynamics is a "heat along the Reeb field" equation ∂h/∂t = c{uh, {uh, h}} in the space of sub-Riemannian metrics on the given contact distribution.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) smooth 3-dimensional manifold equipped with a contact structure, i.e. a smooth rank-2 distribution $\xi \subset TM$ given as the kernel of a 1-form $\alpha$ with $\alpha \wedge d\alpha$ nowhere vanishing. Normalize $\alpha$ (within its conformal class defining $\xi$) so that the associated Reeb vector field $R$ is the unique vector field satisfying $\alpha(R)=1$ and $d\alpha(R,\cdot)=0$.

A sub-Riemannian metric on $(M,\xi)$ is a smooth positive-definite quadratic form $g$ on the bundle $\xi$. Equivalently, it is encoded by its (fiberwise) dual Hamiltonian $h\colon T^*M 	o \mathbb{R}$, the smooth nonnegative function on $T^*M$ that is a positive-semidefinite quadratic form on each cotangent fiber, with kernel exactly the annihilator of $\xi$, and whose restriction to $\xi^*$ is dual to $g$. Let $\{\cdot,\cdot\}$ denote the canonical Poisson bracket on $T^*M$, and let $u\colon T^*M	o \mathbb{R}$ be the linear-on-fibers function $u(\lambda) = \langle \lambda, R(\pi(\lambda))angle$ corresponding to the Reeb field $R$ (with $\pi\colon T^*M	o M$).

A sub-Riemannian metric (or its Hamiltonian $h$) is called Reeb-invariant if the flow of $R$ preserves it; equivalently $\{u,h\}=0$. It is known that smooth Reeb-invariant sub-Riemannian metrics typically do not exist on a given $(M,\xi,\alpha)$.

Question. For an arbitrary closed contact 3-manifold $(M,\xi)$ with chosen contact form $\alpha$, does there exist a natural averaging/diffusion process on the space of sub-Riemannian Hamiltonians on $\xi$ that produces a nontrivial Reeb-invariant limit, possibly only as a generalized (non-smooth) object? More specifically:

(a) Discrete scheme. Do there exist sequences of positive smooth functions $\varepsilon_n, c_n$ on $M$ and an iterative averaging procedure along the Reeb flow such that, starting from any smooth sub-Riemannian Hamiltonian $h_0$, the iterates converge (in a suitable distributional or measure-theoretic sense, after rescaling) to a nonzero limiting Hamiltonian $h_\infty$ with $\{u,h_\infty\}=0$ and with controlled (e.g. measure-valued or current-valued) singularities?

(b) Continuous scheme. Consider the ``heat along the Reeb field'' evolution
$$\frac{\partial h}{\partial t} = c\,\{u h,\,\{u h,\,h\}\},$$
with $c$ a positive (possibly time-dependent) function, in the space of sub-Riemannian Hamiltonians on $\xi$. Does this equation admit, for generic smooth initial data, long-time solutions that converge as $t\to\infty$ (after appropriate rescaling) to a nontrivial generalized Hamiltonian $h_\infty$ that is Reeb-invariant in the sense $\{u,h_\infty\}=0$, with singularities of a controlled type?

Formulate, in either or both of the above settings, the existence and basic regularity of such limiting Reeb-invariant generalized sub-Riemannian metrics on every closed contact 3-manifold.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was posed as an exploratory/imprecise open question about a Ricci-flow-like dynamics on sub-Riemannian metrics on contact 3-manifolds. Subsequent literature on sub-Riemannian curvature, Ricci-type bounds, and tightness for contact 3-manifolds (e.g. work on generalized Ricci curvature bounds, canonical curvature in contact sub-Riemannian geometry, and quantitative tightness via sub-Riemannian methods) develops related geometric tools but does not appear to construct or analyze the proposed Reeb-heat flow ∂h/∂t = c{uh,{uh,h}} or establish convergence to a Reeb-invariant generalized metric. No source found that resolves the question, so it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Generalized Ricci curvature bounds for three dimensional contact subriemannian manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Necessary and sufficient conditions for three-dimensional contact sub-Riemannian manifolds to satisfy a measure contraction property generalizing Ricci curvature bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Related sub-Riemannian Ricci-type bounds have been developed for contact 3-manifolds, but do not address the proposed Reeb-heat dynamics.

status_evidence.title: Quantitative tightness for three-dimensional contact manifolds: a sub-Riemannian approach
status_evidence.snippet: Quantitative estimates for the maximal tight neighbourhood of a Reeb orbit using sub-Riemannian metrics and contact Jacobi curves.
status_evidence.claim: Sub-Riemannian techniques for contact 3-manifolds and Reeb orbits continue to be developed, without resolving the existence of a Reeb-invariant limit of the proposed averaging/heat flow.

status_evidence.title: Sub-Riemannian curvature in contact geometry
status_evidence.snippet: Canonical curvatures for sub-Riemannian contact structures introduced via the Jacobi equation.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational sub-Riemannian curvature framework exists, but the specific Reeb-flow heat equation problem remains posed as an open direction.
